issue: Minimizing a cost function where each parameter must stay inside a box (e.g. rates in [0, 1]) needs a quasi-Newton method that natively supports simple bound constraints; the default unconstrained methods wander out of range.
correct_snippet: res = scipy.optimize.minimize(cost, x0, method="L-BFGS-B", bounds=[(0, 1)] * len(x0))
wrong_snippets: res = scipy.optimize.minimize(cost, x0, method="BFGS", bounds=[(0, 1)] * len(x0))
res = scipy.optimize.minimize(cost, x0, method="Nelder-Mead", bounds=[(0, 1)] * len(x0))
res = scipy.optimize.minimize(cost, x0, method="CG", bounds=[(0, 1)] * len(x0))
probe_question: Which scipy.optimize.minimize method natively supports simple box bounds on the parameters? Reply with ONLY that method name.
